# Micah 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** I said, "Listen, you leaders of Israel! You are supposed to know right from wrong,

**2** But you are the ones who hate good and love evil. You skin My people alive and tear the flesh from their bones.

**3** Yes, you eat My people's flesh, strip their skin, and break their bones. You chop them up like meat for the pot, like chunks of flesh in a stew."

**4** The time will come when they cry out to the LORD for help, but He will not answer. He will hide His face from them because of the evil they have done.

**5** This is what the LORD says about you false prophets who are leading My people astray: You promise peace to those who give you food, but you declare war against anyone who refuses to feed you.

**6** "The night will close over you, cutting off all your visions. Darkness will cover you, putting an end to your predictions. The sun will set on you prophets — your day is done.

**7** You seers will be humiliated, and you fortune-tellers will be disgraced. You will cover your faces in shame, because God refuses to answer you."

**8** But as for me, I am filled with power — with the Spirit of the LORD — and with justice and courage to boldly declare Israel's sin and rebellion.

**9** Listen to me, you leaders of Israel! You hate justice and twist everything that is right.

**10** You are building Jerusalem on a foundation of murder and corruption.

**11** Your leaders make decisions based on bribes. Your priests teach only for pay. Your prophets won't prophesy unless they're paid for it. And then you lean on the LORD and say, "The LORD is with us — nothing bad can happen to us!"

**12** Because of you, Mount Zion will be plowed like an open field. Jerusalem will be reduced to rubble, and the Temple hill will be overgrown with thickets.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **3:2-3**: The imagery is deliberately horrifying — leaders butchering their own people like animals. Micah isn't being poetic; he's being graphic to match the horror of what's actually happening to the poor.

- **3:8**: Micah's 'but as for me' is one of the great prophetic declarations. Everyone around him is corrupt — prophets, priests, politicians — but he stands apart. Not because he's better, but because the Spirit fills him.

- **3:11**: The trifecta of corruption: bribed judges, paid priests, hired prophets — and they all say 'God is with us.' Religious confidence without moral obedience is the most dangerous delusion.

— PNEUMA
